final:
Only one of the four issues needs a code change in this PR: #0, the loosened options type. #1 and #3 point at real behaviour, but the PR didn't introduce either. #2 is a fair test-coverage gap. I didn't change any code or post any replies. The verdicts are in `verdicts.json`, which is valid JSON.

| # | Category | Verdict | Actionable |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | CORRECTNESS | VALID | YES |
| 1 | CORRECTNESS | PARTIALLY_VALID | OPTIONAL |
| 2 | BEST-PRACTICE (tests) | VALID | OPTIONAL |
| 3 | BEST-PRACTICE (tests) | PARTIALLY_VALID | OPTIONAL |

**#0 – options type lets `teamId` be left out (VALID, fix it).**
- This PR added `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` (`insightsBooking.ts:29-34`) and changed the constructor to accept it instead of the stricter type it took before.
- As a result, `{scope: "team", userId, orgId}` with no `teamId` now compiles.
- At runtime, validation fails quietly: the options become `null` (lines 62-63) and the query condition becomes `1=0`, so the caller just gets no results and no error.
- Nothing outside the tests uses the looser type, so going back to the schema-derived type costs nothing.

**#1 – org with no sub-teams drops members' personal bookings (PARTIALLY_VALID).**
- The logic claim is correct. At `insightsBooking.ts:157-162`, if the org has no child teams, the list of member IDs is empty, so direct org members' personal bookings are left out.
- This PR didn't cause it. The same code is in the base version, and it copies the older logic in `packages/features/insights/server/trpc-router.ts:86-101`. The diff only rewrites it as raw SQL.
- It's worth a follow-up, but it's outside the scope of this PR.

**#2 – array binding never runs against the database (VALID, optional).**
- The team-scope and org-scope tests (lines 294-299 and 330-343) only compare the generated SQL objects.
- The one test that actually runs a query uses user scope (lines 480-484), which has no `ANY(${array})` parameter. So the array parameters on service lines 164, 168 and 201 are never checked at runtime.
- The PR description also says the author couldn't run the tests. Running the team and org conditions through `$queryRaw` would be a cheap addition.

**#3 – test rows left behind if an assertion fails (PARTIALLY_VALID).**
- The claim is correct: the rows created at lines 445-466 are only deleted after the assertion (lines 494-500).
- But every test in the file follows the same pattern, and the base version was identical.
- Test data uses unique timestamp and random names, so leftover rows are unlikely to break other tests. This is a clean-up for the whole file, not a problem introduced here.
